ties.name: Breakdown.DichotomyHolds
ties.plain: Finite-dimensional spectral splitting of a compact perturbation

rows.fidelity_note:
Let $\mathcal X$ be a real Hilbert space and let $T_0,C$ be bounded linear operators, with $C$ compact. Let $0\le b\le\alpha<\beta$ and $\|T_0\|\le b$, and write $T=T_0+C$. This assertion says that there are $\alpha<r_1<r_2<\beta$, $K>0$, and a bounded projection $P_u$ commuting with $T$, whose range is finite-dimensional, such that $\|T^n(I-P_u)\|\le Kr_1^n$ and $\|P_ux\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|T^nP_ux\|$ for every natural number $n$ and every $x\in\mathcal X$. The restriction of $T$ maps the range of $P_u$ onto itself. Hence the complement has a controlled forward evolution and the finite-dimensional part has a controlled inverse evolution. The inequalities imply $r_2>0$, so the reciprocal in $r_2^{-n}$ is an ordinary reciprocal. The formulation uses projections and powers rather than a list of complex eigenvalues. It does not impose the existence or size of an unstable eigenvalue. Taking $b=\alpha=e^{-S/4}$ and $\beta=1$ is the application to the period map.

The formal assertion provides a finite-dimensional commuting projection for every compact perturbation of a small bounded operator, without assuming a particular unstable eigenvalue; it is the spectral input rather than the nonlinear stability conclusion.

It is the spectral input rather than the nonlinear stability conclusion.

rows.fidelity_note:
Let $X$ be a complete real Hilbert space. Let $G(t)$, for $t\ge0$, be a strongly continuous semigroup of contractions with $G(0)=I$. Let $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ be symmetric and bounded bilinear, continuous in $\tau>0$ on each pair of vectors, with $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$ and $G(a)K(\tau)=K(a+\tau)$ for $a\ge0$, $\tau>0$. Let $D_\mu$ be a continuous dilation action for $\mu>0$, with $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\nu=D_{\mu\nu}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$. Assume there is a dense set of $f\in X$ for which $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ is compact for every $\tau>0$. The families $G,K,D$ are defined on all real parameters; their analytic bounds and scaling properties hold on the ranges just stated.

Let $\rho$ be a linear isometry of $X$ onto itself commuting with $G,K,D$ for all their real parameters. Let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous, nonzero at some time, and satisfy $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$ with $S>0$. Put $\mathcal S(a)=D_{e^{-a}}G(1-e^{-a})$ and $\widetilde K(a)=D_{e^{-a}}K(1-e^{-a})$. For every $a\le s$, assume the integral below exists and $w(s)=\mathcal S(s-a)w(a)+\int_a^s\widetilde K(s-\sigma)(w(\sigma),w(\sigma))\,d\sigma$.

For every dense linear subspace $C'\subset X$ and $t_0>0$, the assertion supplies an integer $k\ge1$ and a real $\theta$ with $\delta=1-e^{-S/k}\le t_0$ and $e^{-S/(4k)}<\theta<1$. Put $\mu=e^{-S/k}$, $Y=C([0,\delta];X)$ with its supremum norm, $u_n^*(\tau)=D_{(1-\tau)^{-1}}w(nS/k-\log(1-\tau))$, $B_\delta(f,g)(\tau)=\int_0^\tau K(\tau-\sigma)(f(\sigma),g(\sigma))\,d\sigma$, $A_n=2B_\delta(u_n^*,\cdot)$, $\Gamma x(\tau)=G(\tau)x$, and $Lv=D_\mu v(\delta)$. It asserts $\|A_n\|\le1/4$ for all nonnegative integers $n$, and supplies a finite dimensional subspace $V\subset X$, a bounded linear $J:X\to X$ with range in $C'$, and a bounded linear map $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(\mathbb N;Y)\to X\times\ell^\infty(\mathbb N;Y)$. If $(e,z)=\mathcal Rg$, then $e\in V$, $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$ and $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Lz_{n-1}=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. This is a statement of the linear correction on successive intervals; the correction of the datum is $Je\in C'$. The smooth compactly supported space $E$ of the paper is represented by $J(V)$ when $C'$ is the corresponding dense data space. The formula uses only positive $k$, $\mu$, $\theta$ and $1-\tau$, so their reciprocals are ordinary ones. The path operators are formally assigned zero if their required continuous realizations do not exist; the analytic construction for $\delta>0$ proves those realizations before using them.

The product norm controlled by $\mathcal R$ is $\max(\|e\|,\sup_n\|z_n\|_Y)$. A bound for the actual datum correction $Je$ also uses $\|J\|$. The assertion concerns sequences of compact-interval paths, whereas Proposition 4.3 is phrased for a global weighted curve.

This formal statement specifies an implication. Defining the implication does not prove it.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space. Let $G(t)$ be a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, with $G(0)=I$. Let $K(\tau)$ be symmetric bounded bilinear maps, continuous on each pair of arguments for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$, where $C_K\ge0$. For $\mu>0$, assume strongly continuous dilations satisfying $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For every $f$ in a dense subset of $X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with these operators at all their defined real parameters. Let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $S>0$ and $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For every $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to converge and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. The application is $X=\dot H^1_{\rm div}(\mathbb R^3)$ and $D_\mu f(x)=\sqrt\mu f(\sqrt\mu x)$. For every dense real linear subspace $C\subset X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, the conclusion chooses a datum $u(0)\in C$ with $\|u(0)-w(0)\|<\varepsilon$ and a continuous mild curve on $[0,1)$. For some $A\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$, it satisfies $\|D_{1-t}u(t)-w(-\log(1-t))\|\le A(1-t)^\kappa$ for every $0\le t<1$. Here mildness means $u(t)=G(t)u(0)+\int_0^tK(t-r)(u(r),u(r))\,dr$, with each Bochner integral convergent. It does not assert smooth physical representatives or one kinetic-energy bound on the full lifespan, and it does not state the two-sided rate in Theorem 1.1.
rows.name: Breakdown.TransferHolds
rows.annotation: Given a recurrent mild orbit and a compatible isometry, `TransferHolds` asserts that every dense real linear subspace contains initial data arbitrarily close to the profile datum and launching a mild curve on $[0,1)$. After dilation by $1-t$, the curve approaches the profile at rate $(1-t)^\kappa$ for some $\kappa>0$. Taking the subspace of smooth compactly supported solenoidal fields gives the initial-data choice in Theorem 1.1.

rows.fidelity_note:
The formal statement defines an existence assertion on the unit torus. There are a smooth field $u_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ with period one in each coordinate and zero divergence, a real $T>0$, and a continuous mild curve $u$ on $[0,T)$ whose initial state is the Fourier representation of $u_0$, such that $\sup_{0\le t<T}\|u(t)\|=\infty$. The periodic state has coordinates $\sqrt{1+4\pi^2|k|^2}\,\widehat u(k)$, $k\in\mathbb Z^3$, with conjugate symmetry and $k\cdot\widehat u(k)=0$; its norm is the inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm on the unit cell. The zero coefficient is allowed, so this state space does not impose zero mean. The initial-field map returns zero outside its admissible Fourier class; smooth periodic solenoidal data belong to that class. Mild means the heat-plus-quadratic Bochner equation for every $0\le t<T$, with convergent time integrals. The assertion imposes neither $T\le1$ nor either estimate in (1.7), gives no local comparison on $B_{1/16}$, and states unboundedness rather than a specified limit or rate at $T$. It contains no smooth velocity-pressure representative of the curve. The formal statement is only this existence condition; a separate construction proves it from a profile.

rows.fidelity_note:
The formal periodic space represents real divergence-free fields of period one by sequences $a(n)\in\mathbb C^3$, $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, with $\sum_n|a(n)|^2<\infty$, $a(-n)=\overline{a(n)}$ and $n\cdot a(n)=0$. The physical Fourier coefficient is $c(n)=a(n)/(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)^{1/2}$. Its squared norm is $\|u\|^2=\sum_n(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|c(n)|^2$, the inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm; the mean $c(0)$ may be nonzero. The conjugate symmetry is the reality condition and $n\cdot a(n)=0$ is the divergence-free condition. At $n=0$ the latter gives no restriction, which is why nonzero constants are included. The space is a closed real subspace of $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^3;\mathbb C^3)$ and is complete. A nonzero constant has positive formal norm and zero gradient norm, so the mean-zero restriction is essential in (3.16). Equation (3.15) instead uses the homogeneous norm on mean-zero fields of arbitrary period $L$. The distinction matters: the zero Fourier mode contributes to the formal norm, and no variable spatial period is a parameter of an element of the formal space.

The formal unit-torus space uses the inhomogeneous $H^1$ weight $1+4\pi^2|k|^2$ and retains the zero Fourier coefficient; mean zero is not part of that space definition.

Assume, uniformly in $s,y$, $\|D_y^jW(s,y)\|_{\rm op}\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for the three integer orders $j=0,1,2$, and $|\nabla_yq(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$. These assumptions imply $C\ge0$; recurrence and nonvanishing are not required here. The norm on a first derivative is its operator norm; the paper's pointwise matrix norm is the square root of the sum of the squared column lengths, which is at most $\sqrt3$ times this norm.

Put $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and let $\chi$ be the fixed smooth cutoff with $0\le\chi\le1$, equal to one for $|x-a|\le1/16$ and zero for $|x-a|\ge1/8$. For $T>0$, $t<T$, set $\ell=T-t$, $s=-\log(\ell/T)$ and $g(x)=\ell^{-1/2}W(s,(x-a)/\sqrt\ell)$. Define $A_g(x)=\int_0^1\sigma\,g(a+\sigma(x-a))\times(x-a)\,d\sigma$, $\bar u(x)=\chi(x)g(x)+\nabla\chi(x)\times A_g(x)$, and $f(y)=\sqrt\ell\,\bar u(a+\sqrt\ell\,y)$. Thus $f$ is the cutoff expressed in similarity coordinates; its inner and outer radii are $1/(16\sqrt\ell)$ and $1/(8\sqrt\ell)$. Put $x_a=a+(3/32)e_1$ and $\bar p(x)=\chi(x)\ell^{-1}[q(s,(x-a)/\sqrt\ell)-q(s,(x_a-a)/\sqrt\ell)]$.

Assume, for every profile satisfying the displayed hypotheses and every $T>0$, that $\bar u,\bar p$ are smooth on $(-\infty,T)\times\mathbb R^3$, the velocity is solenoidal, both vanish for $|x-a|\ge1/8$, and the velocity equals $g$ on $|x-a|\le1/16$; this property is proved separately. For every $\varepsilon>0$, the formal statement gives $\ell_0>0$ such that, for every $T>0$ and $t<T$ with $T-t<\ell_0$, $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_{i=1}^3|\partial_i(W(s,y)-f(y))|^2\,dy\le\varepsilon$. The exported conclusion gives no power-law rate, no estimate for every prescribed $r>0$, and no bound by the particular constant in (5.2). ties.plain: The bilinear Navier–Stokes operator

assessments.fidelity_note:
For each $\tau>0$, the formal definition chooses a bounded real bilinear map $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ satisfying $\langle K(\tau)(u,v),\psi\rangle_X=-\tfrac12\int[(u\cdot\nabla)v+(v\cdot\nabla)u]\cdot\Phi_\tau\psi$ for every $u,v,\psi\in X$. The space $X$ is represented by real solenoidal frequency classes $g=2\pi|\xi|\hat u$ in $L^2$, and physical velocities lie in $L^6$. The test field $\Phi_\tau\psi$ has frequency transform $2\pi|\xi|e^{-4\pi^2\tau|\xi|^2}g_\psi$, so for smooth fields it represents $-\Delta e^{\tau\Delta}\psi$. If $\tau\le0$, or if no bounded bilinear map with the displayed property exists, the definition assigns the zero map. The supplied existence theorem proves that such a map exists for every $\tau>0$. The value at $\tau=0$ is consequently a convention; when it occurs at the endpoint of a time integral it is a single null-time value. The positive-time estimate and symmetry are separate statements.

The formal operator on all of $X$ is specified through the symmetrized transport pairing. The paper defines it directly through projected transport.

Let $\varphi:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be smooth, compactly supported and divergence-free, let $v\in X$, and let $\tau>0$. Reconstruct $v$ as an $L^6$ velocity and its coordinate derivatives as $L^2$ fields. The formal statement proves $K(\tau)(J\varphi,v)=-\tfrac12H_\tau[(\varphi\cdot\nabla)v+(v\cdot\nabla)\varphi]$, as an equality in $X$. ties.name: Breakdown.Freq.trilinear_holds
ties.plain: Integrability of the transport pairing

rows.fidelity_note:
The formal theorem supplies a constant $C\in\mathbb R$ such that, for all $u,v\in X=\dot H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb R^3)$ and all fields $w\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)\cap L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, meaning fields with a measurable representative and finite second and sixth integral norms, the integrand $(u\cdot\nabla)v\cdot w$ is integrable and its integral has absolute value at most $C\|u\|_X\|v\|_X\sqrt{\|w\|_{L^2}\|w\|_{L^6}}$. The state for $u$ is $2\pi|\xi|\widehat u(\xi)$; the velocity is reconstructed in $L^6$, and each derivative of $v$ is reconstructed in $L^2$ by the multiplier $i\xi_j/|\xi|$ on its state. Division at $\xi=0$ is assigned zero, a value at a set of measure zero. All products and integrals are insensitive to choices of representatives. This is the transport-pairing estimate used to construct $K$ by duality. Its conclusion is integrability and a bound for the scalar pairing, rather than an explicit assertion that the vector field $(u\cdot\nabla)v$ belongs to $L^{3/2}$ or decomposes into $L^1+L^2$.

The formal theorem bounds and proves integrability of the scalar transport pairing against $L^2\cap L^6$ fields. It does not state the vector-valued $L^{3/2}$ membership or the $L^1+L^2$ decomposition used in this sentence.

ties.name: Breakdown.VarConstIntegralStatement
ties.plain: Continuity of the Duhamel integral

rows.fidelity_note:
Let $\mathcal X$ be a real Banach space. Write $G(t)$ for a strongly continuous contraction semigroup on $t\ge0$, and let $K(\tau)$ be bounded symmetric real bilinear maps on $\mathcal X$, continuous in $\tau>0$ on each pair of arguments. Assume $G(t)K(\tau)=K(t+\tau)$ for $t\ge0,\tau>0$, and $\|K(\tau)(u,v)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}\|u\|\|v\|$ for $0<\tau\le1$. This is the assertion that, if $a\le b$, $u,v:\mathbb R\to\mathcal X$ are continuous on $[a,b]$, and $\|u(s)\|\le M$, $\|v(s)\|\le N$ there, then $K(t-s)(u(s),v(s))$ is Bochner integrable from $a$ to $t$ for every $t\in[a,b]$, and its integral is continuous in $t$ on $[a,b]$. In addition, when $t-a\le1$, its norm is at most $4C_K(t-a)^{1/4}MN$. Such finite $M,N$ exist by compactness of $[a,b]$. Integrability and continuity have no restriction on $b-a$. The interval of length zero is allowed, with integral zero. Values of the curves outside $[a,b]$ and the value of $K(0)$ do not affect the conclusion.

For continuous inputs on a compact time interval the formal statement gives Bochner integrability and continuity of the Duhamel integral. It applies on $[a,t]$ for each $t<b$.

rows.fidelity_note: For $a<b$, a mild curve is a continuous $u:[a,b]\to X$ satisfying $u(t)=G(t-a)u(a)+\int_a^tK(t-s)(u(s),u(s))\,ds$ for every $a\le t\le b$, with each integral Bochner integrable. In the whole-space application $G(t)=e^{t\Delta}$ and $X=\dot H^1_{\rm div}(\mathbb R^3)$. The equation includes the right endpoint. The curve has arbitrary values outside the interval, and the formal condition is vacuous for $b<a$. For $b=a$ the integral is zero and $G(0)=I$.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.V
ties.plain: The periodic Fourier space

rows.fidelity_note:
The formal periodic space represents real divergence-free fields of period one by sequences $a(n)\in\mathbb C^3$, $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, with $\sum_n|a(n)|^2<\infty$, $a(-n)=\overline{a(n)}$ and $n\cdot a(n)=0$. The physical Fourier coefficient is $c(n)=a(n)/(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)^{1/2}$. Its squared norm is $\|u\|^2=\sum_n(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|c(n)|^2$, the inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm; the mean $c(0)$ may be nonzero. The conjugate symmetry is the reality condition and $n\cdot a(n)=0$ is the divergence-free condition. At $n=0$ the latter gives no restriction, which is why nonzero constants are included. The space is a closed real subspace of $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^3;\mathbb C^3)$ and is complete. A nonzero constant has positive formal norm and zero gradient norm, so the mean-zero restriction is essential in (3.16). Equation (3.15) instead uses the homogeneous norm on mean-zero fields of arbitrary period $L$. The distinction matters: the zero Fourier mode contributes to the formal norm, and no variable spatial period is a parameter of an element of the formal space.

The formal periodic space uses the inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm on the fixed unit torus and permits a nonzero mean.

rows.fidelity_note:
The formal periodic space represents real divergence-free fields of period one by sequences $a(n)\in\mathbb C^3$, $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, with $\sum_n|a(n)|^2<\infty$, $a(-n)=\overline{a(n)}$ and $n\cdot a(n)=0$. For finite real numbers $a,b$, a curve $u$ defined for all real times with values in this periodic space is a mild solution on $[a,b)$ if it is continuous there and, for every $t\in[a,b)$, the integral $\int_a^tK_{\mathbb T}(t-s)(u(s),u(s))\,ds$ is Bochner integrable in the formal periodic space and $u(t)=e^{(t-a)\Delta}u(a)+\int_a^tK_{\mathbb T}(t-s)(u(s),u(s))\,ds$. Here the heat operator has Fourier multiplier $e^{-4\pi^2(t-a)|n|^2}$, and $K_{\mathbb T}(\tau)$ is the symmetrized projected transport operator for $\tau>0$, with value zero for $\tau\le0$. No behavior at $b$ or outside $[a,b)$ is required. This definition concerns the unit torus with its inhomogeneous norm, whereas §3.6 works in mean-zero homogeneous spaces at arbitrary period.

The same Duhamel form is imposed on a curve in that larger periodic Fourier space; zero mean is not part of the condition.

assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space. Let $G(t)$ be a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, with $G(0)=I$. Let $K(\tau)$ be symmetric bounded bilinear maps, continuous on each pair of arguments for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$, where $C_K\ge0$. For $\mu>0$, assume strongly continuous dilations satisfying $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For every $f$ in a dense subset of $X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with these operators at all their defined real parameters. Let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $S>0$ and $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For every $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to converge and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. The application is $X=\dot H^1_{\rm div}(\mathbb R^3)$ and $D_\mu f(x)=\sqrt\mu f(\sqrt\mu x)$. For every dense real linear subspace $C\subset X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, the conclusion chooses a datum $u(0)\in C$ with $\|u(0)-w(0)\|<\varepsilon$ and a continuous mild curve on $[0,1)$. For some $A\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$, it satisfies $\|D_{1-t}u(t)-w(-\log(1-t))\|\le A(1-t)^\kappa$ for every $0\le t<1$. Here mildness means $u(t)=G(t)u(0)+\int_0^tK(t-r)(u(r),u(r))\,dr$, with each Bochner integral convergent. Proposition 2.1 instead quantifies over every nearby prescribed datum, retains one fixed finite-dimensional correction space and states two-sided physical bounds. Those claims are not all present in this exported transfer assertion.

rows.fidelity_note:
Let $X$ be a complete real Hilbert space. Let $G(t)$, for $t\ge0$, be a strongly continuous semigroup of contractions with $G(0)=I$. Let $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ be symmetric and bounded bilinear, continuous in $\tau>0$ on each pair of vectors, with $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$ and $G(a)K(\tau)=K(a+\tau)$ for $a\ge0$, $\tau>0$. Let $D_\mu$ be a continuous dilation action for $\mu>0$, with $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\nu=D_{\mu\nu}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$. Assume there is a dense set of $f\in X$ for which $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ is compact for every $\tau>0$. The families $G,K,D$ are defined on all real parameters; their analytic bounds and scaling properties hold on the ranges just stated.

Let $\rho$ be a linear isometry of $X$ onto itself commuting with $G,K,D$ for all their real parameters. Let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous, nonzero at some time, and satisfy $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$ with $S>0$. Put $\mathcal S(a)=D_{e^{-a}}G(1-e^{-a})$ and $\widetilde K(a)=D_{e^{-a}}K(1-e^{-a})$. For every $a\le s$, assume the integral below exists and $w(s)=\mathcal S(s-a)w(a)+\int_a^s\widetilde K(s-\sigma)(w(\sigma),w(\sigma))\,d\sigma$.

For every dense linear subspace $C'\subset X$ and $t_0>0$, the assertion supplies an integer $k\ge1$ and a real $\theta$ with $\delta=1-e^{-S/k}\le t_0$ and $e^{-S/(4k)}<\theta<1$. Put $\mu=e^{-S/k}$, $Y=C([0,\delta];X)$ with its supremum norm, $u_n^*(\tau)=D_{(1-\tau)^{-1}}w(nS/k-\log(1-\tau))$, $B_\delta(f,g)(\tau)=\int_0^\tau K(\tau-\sigma)(f(\sigma),g(\sigma))\,d\sigma$, $A_n=2B_\delta(u_n^*,\cdot)$, $\Gamma x(\tau)=G(\tau)x$, and $Lv=D_\mu v(\delta)$. It asserts $\|A_n\|\le1/4$ for all nonnegative integers $n$, and supplies a finite dimensional subspace $V\subset X$, a bounded linear $J:X\to X$ with range in $C'$, and a bounded linear map $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(\mathbb N;Y)\to X\times\ell^\infty(\mathbb N;Y)$. If $(e,z)=\mathcal Rg$, then $e\in V$, $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$ and $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Lz_{n-1}=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. This is a statement of the linear correction on successive intervals; the correction of the datum is $Je\in C'$. The smooth compactly supported space $E$ of the paper is represented by $J(V)$ when $C'$ is the corresponding dense data space. The formula uses only positive $k$, $\mu$, $\theta$ and $1-\tau$, so their reciprocals are ordinary ones. The path operators are formally assigned zero if their required continuous realizations do not exist; the analytic construction for $\delta>0$ proves those realizations before using them.

The product norm controlled by $\mathcal R$ is $\max(\|e\|,\sup_n\|z_n\|_Y)$. A bound for the actual datum correction $Je$ also uses $\|J\|$. The assertion concerns sequences of compact-interval paths, whereas Proposition 4.3 is phrased for a global weighted curve.

A separate theorem proves this statement from the spectral dichotomy.

The formal statement produces a finite-dimensional correction parameter space, a lift into any dense linear data class, and a bounded right inverse for the linear recurrence. It does not yet state this nonlinear stability conclusion or its constants.

ties.name: Breakdown.Freq.testDense_holds
ties.plain: Density of compact solenoidal fields

rows.fidelity_note:
Let $X=\{g\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3):g(-\xi)=\overline{g(\xi)},\ \xi\cdot g(\xi)=0\text{ a.e.}\}$, with its real $L^2$ Hilbert norm. For a smooth compactly supported divergence-free field $\varphi$, write $J\varphi$ for its frequency representation $2\pi|\xi|\hat\varphi$. The formal statement proves that the real linear span of these $J\varphi$ is dense in $X$. It also proves density in the graph norm of the negative Laplacian: if $g,h\in X$ satisfy $h(\xi)=4\pi^2|\xi|^2g(\xi)$ almost everywhere, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is such a $\varphi$ with $\|J\varphi-g\|_X<\varepsilon$ and $\|J(-\Delta\varphi)-h\|_X<\varepsilon$. A separate formal statement shows that every element of the indicated span is itself represented by one compact smooth divergence-free field. Thus the first conclusion gives the density used in §3.1; the graph approximation is additional information.

The formal density result permits approximation of every element of $X$ to every positive tolerance by the span of compact smooth solenoidal fields; it also gives approximation in the graph norm of the Laplacian.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup
ties.plain: Smooth periodic data with unbounded mild H¹ flow

assessments.fidelity_note:
The formal statement defines an existence assertion on the unit torus. There are a smooth field $u_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ with period one in each coordinate and zero divergence, a real $T>0$, and a continuous mild curve $u$ on $[0,T)$ whose initial state is the Fourier representation of $u_0$, such that $\sup_{0\le t<T}\|u(t)\|=\infty$. The periodic state has coordinates $\sqrt{1+4\pi^2|k|^2}\,\widehat u(k)$, $k\in\mathbb Z^3$, with conjugate symmetry and $k\cdot\widehat u(k)=0$; its norm is the inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm on the unit cell. The zero coefficient is allowed, so this state space does not impose zero mean. The initial-field map returns zero outside its admissible Fourier class; smooth periodic solenoidal data belong to that class. Mild means the heat-plus-quadratic Bochner equation for every $0\le t<T$, with convergent time integrals. The assertion imposes neither $T\le1$ nor either estimate in (2.6), gives no local comparison on $B_{1/16}$, and states unboundedness rather than a specified limit or rate at $T$. It contains no smooth velocity-pressure representative of the curve. This is the existence condition; a separate construction proves it from a profile.

This formal existence condition contains no profile premise. A separate construction obtains it from a profile and supplies an unbounded periodic mild curve.

Let $V$ be the real Hilbert space of unit-periodic solenoidal Fourier states, with norm squared $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat u(k)|^2$; zero mean is not required. Fix $T>0$, $0<\lambda<1$, $0<\theta<1$, $c_0>0$, and $Z\in\mathbb R$. For every integer $n\ge0$, let $u_n$, $\bar u_n$ and $z_n$ be continuous $V$-valued maps on $[0,1-\lambda]$. Assume $\|\bar u_n(s)\|\ge c_0$ for all $n,s$, $\sup_s\|z_n(s)\|\le Z$ for all $n$, and $u_n=\bar u_n+\theta^n z_n$. Put $a_n=T-T\lambda^n$ and $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$. On $[a_n,a_{n+1})$, define the joined curve by $U(t)=\mu_n^{-1/4}u_n((t-a_n)/\mu_n)$. The formal statement concludes that $\{\|U(t)\|:0\le t<T\}$ is unbounded above. The powers $\lambda^n$ and $\theta^n$ have nonnegative integer exponents. The positive parameters ensure that all divisions and logarithms used to select the interval are legitimate on $[0,T)$. Continuous pieces are extended by their endpoint values when evaluated outside their interval; these values are irrelevant on the stated pieces. No matching of endpoints or mild equation is assumed here, so neither continuity of $U$ nor its being a solution is part of this conclusion. This is a geometric unboundedness criterion, stated as a proposition; its proof is a separate theorem.

The formal criterion proves unboundedness of the joined norm from a uniformly nonzero approximate sequence and a geometrically decaying correction. It contains no local spatial comparison or sharp rate for a solution.

**Lemma 3.3.** Let $a\le b$, and let $u,v:[a,b]\to\mathcal X$ be continuous. Then for every $t\in[a,b]$ the map $t'\mapsto K(t-t')(u(t'),v(t'))$ is integrable on $[a,t]$, and the map $$
t\mapsto\int_a^t K(t-t')(u(t'),v(t'))\,dt'
$$ is continuous on $[a,b]$.

ties.plain: Continuity of the Duhamel integral

assessments.fidelity_note: Let $\mathcal X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau)$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps, continuous for each fixed pair of arguments when $\tau>0$. Assume $G(s)K(\tau)(u,v)=K(s+\tau)(u,v)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. If $a\le b$ and $u,v$ are continuous on $[a,b]$, with $\|u(s)\|\le M$ and $\|v(s)\|\le N$ throughout, then $I(t)=\int_a^tK(t-s)(u(s),v(s))\,ds$ is Bochner integrable for every $t\in[a,b]$ and continuous in $t$. When $t-a\le1$, $\|I(t)\|\le4C_K(t-a)^{1/4}MN$. Such $M,N$ exist by compactness. This includes Lemma 3.3 and an additional short-time estimate under a weaker lag-bound hypothesis. This linked definition states the assertion.

ties.name: Breakdown.PieceOperatorStatement
ties.plain: Uniform bounds for the Duhamel operator on a compact time interval

rows.fidelity_note: Let $\mathcal X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau)$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps, continuous for each fixed pair of arguments when $\tau>0$. Assume $G(s)K(\tau)(u,v)=K(s+\tau)(u,v)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $T>0$, the formal assertion identifies $B_T:C([0,T];\mathcal X)^2\to C([0,T];\mathcal X)$ by $B_T(f,h)(t)=\int_0^tK(t-s)(f(s),h(s))\,ds$ and proves bounded bilinearity; $\|B_T\|\le4C_KT^{1/4}$ when $T\le1$. It also identifies $\Gamma_T:\mathcal X\to C([0,T];\mathcal X)$ by $\Gamma_Tx(t)=G(t)x$, with norm at most one. Translating time gives the integral operator in Lemma 3.4; invertibility of $I-2B_T(f,\cdot)$ on an arbitrary interval is a further conclusion. The linked definition states these operator properties.

rows.annotation: Let $\mathcal X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau)$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps, continuous for each fixed pair of arguments when $\tau>0$. Assume $G(s)K(\tau)(u,v)=K(s+\tau)(u,v)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. Let $a\le m\le t$ and let $u$ be continuous on $[a,t]$. If its quadratic Duhamel integrals are Bochner integrable and $u(r)=G(r-a)u(a)+\int_a^rK(r-s)(u(s),u(s))\,ds$ holds for $r=m,t$, the formal assertion gives Bochner integrability on $[m,t]$ and $u(t)=G(t-m)u(m)+\int_m^tK(t-s)(u(s),u(s))\,ds$. Formula (3.13) permits independent factors $f,h$ and assumes the original identity throughout an interval. The formal implication uses the quadratic factors $u,u$ and only two times. This linked definition states the implication.

ties.name: Breakdown.UniqueStatement
ties.plain: Uniqueness of mild solutions

rows.fidelity_note: Let $\mathcal X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau)$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps, continuous for each fixed pair of arguments when $\tau>0$. Assume $G(s)K(\tau)(u,v)=K(s+\tau)(u,v)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. Two continuous curves satisfying $u(t)=G(t-a)u(a)+\int_a^tK(t-s)(u(s),u(s))\,ds$, with each integral Bochner integrable, agree throughout their common $[a,b]$ if their values at $a$ agree. The formal assertion also gives this conclusion on $[a,b)$ and imposes no smallness of the datum or interval. It includes the uniqueness clause of Lemma 3.5 under a kernel estimate required only at lags at most one. This linked definition states the assertion.

ties.name: Breakdown.advectionPairing
ties.plain: Transport paired with a test field

rows.fidelity_note: The formal expression is $\int_{\mathbb R^3}((u\cdot\nabla)u)\cdot\psi\,dx$. For smooth solenoidal $u$ and a smooth compactly supported $\psi$, its negative equals $\int\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_i\psi_j\,dx$ by integration by parts. The paper defines a general three-field tensor contraction; the linked definition instead gives this two-field transport pairing and does not assert the integration-by-parts theorem.
rows.name: Breakdown.advectionPairing
rows.plain: Transport paired with a test field
rows.annotation: `advectionPairing` uses the physical advection integral $\int ((u\cdot\nabla)u)\cdot\psi$. For smooth solenoidal $u$ and compactly supported smooth $\psi$, integration by parts moves the derivative to $\psi$ and yields the negative of the tensor contraction in the passage.

ties.plain: Fourier coefficients on the unit torus

rows.fidelity_note: For a field $f:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ and $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, the formal definition is $\hat f(n)=\int_{[0,1]^3}e^{-2\pi i n\cdot x}f(x)\,dx$. rows.fidelity_note: The formal periodic space consists of real solenoidal fields of period one with norm $\|u\|_{H^1}^2=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|\hat u(n)|^2$; the mean may be nonzero. assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space. Suppose $G(t)$, $t\ge0$, is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K(\tau)$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous on each pair of arguments for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $\mu>0$, suppose the dilations are strongly continuous, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For a dense set of $f\in X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with $G,K,D$, including their assigned values at all real parameters. Let $S>0$ and let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to exist and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. Fix an integer $k\ge1$, set $\mu=e^{-S/k}$ and $L=1-\mu$, and define $a_n(\sigma)=D_{(1-\sigma)^{-1}}w(nS/k-\log(1-\sigma))$ for $0\le\sigma\le L$. The formal assertion states that $a_n$ is a continuous mild solution on $[0,L]$, $D_\mu a_n(L)=a_{n+1}(0)$ and $a_{n+k}=\rho a_n$. If $\|w(s)\|\le M$ for every real $s$, it also states $\|a_n\|_\infty\le e^{S/(4k)}M$. The paper's formula instead holds on a whole period for every $0\le\sigma<1$: $u^*(1-\lambda^n+\lambda^n\sigma)=\rho_R^nD_{\lambda^{-n}}u^*(\sigma)$, $\lambda=e^{-S}$. The formal assertion states matching and a one-period shift for the short pieces, without that whole-period identity as a conclusion.

assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space. Suppose $G(t)$, $t\ge0$, is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K(\tau)$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous on each pair of arguments for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $\mu>0$, suppose the dilations are strongly continuous, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For $\mu>0$, suppose the dilations are strongly continuous, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For a dense set of $f\in X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with $G,K,D$, including their assigned values at all real parameters. Let $S>0$ and let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to exist and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. Fix an integer $k\ge1$, put $\mu=e^{-S/k}$, $L=1-\mu$ and $a_n(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(nS/k-\log(1-t))$ on $[0,L]$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ define $A_nz(t)=2\int_0^tK(t-r)(a_n(r),z(r))\,dr$, $\Gamma x(t)=G(t)x$ and $Ev=D_\mu v(L)$. The formal assertion assumes $\|A_n\|\le1/4$ for every $n$, and states that $I-A_n$ is invertible with inverse norm at most $4/3$. With $S_n=E(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$, $\mathcal M=\rho^{-1}S_{k-1}\cdots S_0$ and $\mathcal M_0=\rho^{-1}(D_\mu G(L))^k$, it states $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, compactness of $\mathcal M-\mathcal M_0$, and $\|\mathcal M_0\|\le e^{-S/4}$. rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. For $T>0$, put $Y=C([0,T];X)$ with its supremum norm and $B_T(f,g)(t)=\int_0^tK(t-r)(f(r),g(r))\,dr$. The formal definition selects the bounded bilinear map with this formula, assigning zero if no such map exists. The compact-interval operator theorem establishes existence, so the assigned zero value is unused under these hypotheses. Only values inside $[0,T]$ are integrated; the value at lag zero affects a set of measure zero. The paper defines $\mathcal B$ on continuous curves on $[0,1)$. For each $0<T<1$, restricting those curves gives exactly this integral formula on $[0,T]$. The formal object has a compact-interval domain, so it does not by itself define one operator on the whole half-open interval.
rows.name: Breakdown.HeatBilinear.pieceBil
rows.annotation: `pieceBil` is the same Duhamel integral on a closed interval $[0,L]$. At $t$ it integrates the bilinear kernel of lag $t-s$ applied to the two curve values at $s$. The kernel bound of order $(t-s)^{-3/4}$ makes the endpoint integrable. Applying this on each compact subinterval underlies the paper's formula on $[0,1)$.

assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $k\ge1$, $\theta>0$, and let $\rho:X\to X$ be a surjective linear isometry. Let $A_n:Y\to Y$, $\Gamma:X\to Y$, $E:Y\to X$ and $J,P:X\to X$ be bounded linear maps. Assume $I-A_n$ have uniformly bounded inverses. Set $S_n=E(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$ and $M=\rho^{-1}S_{k-1}\cdots S_0$, and assume $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, $P^2=P$, $PM=MP$, $PJ=P$. For $0\le r_1<\theta^k<r_2$, require $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$, $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for all $n\ge0,x\in X$, and surjectivity of $M$ on $\operatorname{ran}P$. The formal assertion supplies a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to X\times\ell^\infty(Y)$. For $(e,z)=\mathcal Rg$, it requires $e\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$ and $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. The product norm is $\max(\|e\|,\sup_n\|z_n\|_Y)$. In the fluid application $Y=C([0,L];X)$. The paper's (4.12) specifies one curve $v$ with a prescribed global source $g$ and initial vector $\chi$. The formal assertion instead solves a bounded sequence of coupled interval equations and chooses a projected initial coordinate. It does not state (4.12) for an arbitrary prescribed $\chi$.

assessments.fidelity_note: For a bounded linear operator $M$ on a real normed space, a real $\theta$, a prescribed source sequence $c_n$ and an initial value $x_0$, the formal definition is $x_{n+1}=\theta^{-1}(Mx_n+c_n)$ for natural $n$. It has no boundedness or decay conclusion. At $\theta=0$ division is assigned zero; the dichotomy arguments impose $\theta>0$. For $\theta>0$, the substitutions $\chi_n=\theta^nx_n$ and $f_n=\theta^nc_n$ yield $\chi_{n+1}=M\chi_n+f_n$. The paper's (4.13) instead defines rescaled curves $v_n,g_n$ and derives its forcing $f_n$ from a global source. The recurrence definition presupposes its sequence $c_n$ and defines none of those physical-to-period maps. It is a related discrete formulation only.

assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space. Suppose $G(t)$, $t\ge0$, is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K(\tau)$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous on each pair of arguments for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $\mu>0$, suppose the dilations are strongly continuous, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For a dense set of $f\in X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with $G,K,D$, including their assigned values at all real parameters. Let $S>0$ and let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to exist and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. For a dense linear subspace $C\subset X$ and $t_0>0$, the formal assertion chooses $k\ge1$, $\mu=e^{-S/k}$, $L=1-\mu\le t_0$ and $\mu^{1/4}<\theta<1$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ with its supremum norm, set $a_n(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(nS/k-\log(1-t))$, $A_nz(t)=2\int_0^tK(t-r)(a_n(r),z(r))\,dr$, $\Gamma x(t)=G(t)x$, and $Ev=D_\mu v(L)$. It gives $\|A_n\|\le1/4$, a finite-dimensional $V\subset X$, a bounded linear $J:X\to X$ with range in $C$, and a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to X\times\ell^\infty(Y)$. Writing $(e,z)=\mathcal Rg$, the conclusions are $e\in V$, $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$ and $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. The physical datum correction is $Je\in J(V)$; its bound also uses $\|J\|$. The bounded source sequence $g_n\in Y$ is an input to this inverse. The paper's (4.15) estimates an interval source and a derived endpoint forcing in terms of the norm of one global $C_\kappa$ curve. The formal assertion contains no such global source norm, no formula for that derived forcing, and no claim of the displayed constant's independence from $\chi$.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. Assume $K(\tau)(f,g)$ depends continuously on $\tau>0$, $G(s)K(\tau)(f,g)=K(s+\tau)(f,g)$ for $s\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. Let $0<T\le1$, $a,v\in C([0,T];X)$ and $x\in X$. Write $B_T(f,g)(t)=\int_0^tK(t-r)(f(r),g(r))\,dr$. If $a(t)=G(t)a(0)+B_T(a,a)(t)$ and $v(t)=G(t)x+2B_T(a,v)(t)+B_T(v,v)(t)$, the formal assertion concludes $v(0)=x$ and $a+v$ is a continuous mild solution on $[0,T]$, including integrability of its Duhamel term. The quoted paper assertion is an equivalence on $[0,1)$. The formal assertion gives the implication from the perturbation identity to an exact mild sum on a closed interval of length at most one; it does not state the converse.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $M,P$ bounded linear operators with $P^2=P$ and $PM=MP$, and $0\le r_1<\Theta<r_2$. Assume $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$, $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for every natural $n$ and $x\in X$, and surjectivity of $M$ on $\operatorname{ran}P$. The formal assertion supplies a bounded linear $U:\ell^\infty(X)\to X$ with $PUc=Uc$ and a constant $K\prime$. If $Px_0=Uc$, the normalized recurrence $x_{n+1}=\Theta^{-1}(Mx_n+c_n)$ satisfies $\|x_n\|\le K\prime(\|x_0\|+\|c\|_\infty)$ for all $n$. Finite rank of $P$ is not assumed here. The paper derives a forced recurrence from a global source curve and identifies a finite-dimensional complementary subspace. This formal assertion solves the normalized discrete problem once its operators and bounds are supplied. It does not derive that recurrence from the physical-time equation or impose finite rank.

rows.fidelity_note: The linked theorem takes the spectral dichotomy assertion as a premise: compact perturbations of small operators on real Hilbert spaces admit a commuting finite-rank projection with geometric forward and inverse bounds. Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space. Suppose $G(t)$, $t\ge0$, is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K(\tau)$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous on each pair of arguments for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $\mu>0$, suppose the dilations are strongly continuous, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For a dense set of $f\in X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with $G,K,D$, including their assigned values at all real parameters. Let $S>0$ and let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to exist and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. For a dense linear subspace $C\subset X$ and $t_0>0$, the formal assertion chooses $k\ge1$, $\mu=e^{-S/k}$, $L=1-\mu\le t_0$ and $\mu^{1/4}<\theta<1$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ with its supremum norm, set $a_n(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(nS/k-\log(1-t))$, $A_nz(t)=2\int_0^tK(t-r)(a_n(r),z(r))\,dr$, $\Gamma x(t)=G(t)x$, and $Ev=D_\mu v(L)$. It gives $\|A_n\|\le1/4$, a finite-dimensional $V\subset X$, a bounded linear $J:X\to X$ with range in $C$, and a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to X\times\ell^\infty(Y)$. Writing $(e,z)=\mathcal Rg$, the conclusions are $e\in V$, $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$ and $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. The physical datum correction is $Je\in J(V)$; its bound also uses $\|J\|$. The paper's correction space is represented by $J(V)$ when $C$ consists of smooth compactly supported solenoidal fields. rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. Assume $K(\tau)(f,g)$ depends continuously on $\tau>0$, $G(s)K(\tau)(f,g)=K(s+\tau)(f,g)$ for $s\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. Assume a dense set of $f\in X$ has $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. For $0<T\le1$ and every continuous $a:[0,T]\to X$, the formal theorem proves compactness of $g\mapsto\int_0^TK(T-r)(a(r),g(r))\,dr$ from $C([0,T];X)$ to $X$. Composing with the bounded map from initial datum to a linearized trajectory supplies the compact endpoint correction. The paper proves compactness by a particular weakly convergent sequence over the first period; that sequence argument is not the theorem's statement.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space and $M=T_0+C$, where $T_0,C$ are bounded linear operators, $C$ is compact and $\|T_0\|\le b\le\alpha<\beta$ with $b\ge0$. The formal assertion supplies $\alpha<r_1<r_2<\beta$, $K>0$ and a bounded finite-rank projection $P$ such that $PM=MP$, $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$ and $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for all natural $n$ and $x\in X$; $M$ maps $\operatorname{ran}P$ onto itself. The last two properties make the restricted operator $M_{\mathrm u}$ invertible. The linked theorem proves this assertion. For $b=\alpha=e^{-S/4}$ and $\beta=1$, choose $r_1<\Theta<r_2$. The resulting projection and invertibility give the clause in Lemma 4.5, while the geometric estimates provide additional quantitative information. The theorem applies to every such compact perturbation, independently of its origin as a fluid period map.

ties.name: Breakdown.Spectral.Complexification.norm_map_le
ties.plain: Norm under complexification

rows.fidelity_note: For a bounded real-linear operator $T$ on a real inner-product space $X$, the formal theorem proves $\|T_{\mathbb C}\|\le\|T\|$. Here $T_{\mathbb C}(x+iy)=Tx+iTy$ and $\|x+iy\|^2=\|x\|^2+\|y\|^2$. The paper asserts equality of the real and complex operator norms. Its reverse inequality follows by restriction to the isometric copy $x\mapsto x+i0$ and is not the linked theorem's conclusion.

ties.name: Breakdown.Spectral.finite_spectrum_outside
ties.plain: Finitely many spectral points outside the norm bound

rows.fidelity_note: For bounded linear $T_0,C$ on a complex Banach space with $C$ compact and $\|T_0\|\le b<r$, the formal theorem proves that $\{z\in\sigma(T_0+C):|z|\ge r\}$ is finite. For the period map, $b=e^{-S/4}$ bounds the free part. The paper's sentence instead gives invariance of the essential spectral radius and identifies exterior spectral points as poles of finite algebraic multiplicity, using Engel–Nagel, Chapter IV, §1.20 and (1.16). Those intermediate assertions are not the linked theorem's conclusion.

ties.name: Breakdown.Spectral.specProj
ties.plain: Riesz projection onto spectrum inside a circle

rows.fidelity_note: For a bounded operator $T$ on a complex normed space and a real $r$, the formal definition is $Q=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_{|z|=r}(zI-T)^{-1}\,dz$, counterclockwise. A nonexistent bounded inverse and a nonintegrable contour integral are assigned zero. If the space is complete, $r>0$ and the circle lies in the resolvent set, this is the spectral projection for the spectrum inside the circle. The paper selects the exterior spectrum; with $T=\mathcal M$ and $r=\Theta$, its projection is $P=I-Q$.

ties.name: Breakdown.StepDataStatement
ties.plain: Interval splitting and right-inverse data for the linearized equation

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space. Suppose $G(t)$, $t\ge0$, is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K(\tau)$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous on each pair of arguments for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $\mu>0$, suppose the dilations are strongly continuous, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For a dense set of $f\in X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with $G,K,D$, including their assigned values at all real parameters. Let $S>0$ and let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to exist and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. For a dense linear subspace $C\subset X$ and $t_0>0$, the formal assertion chooses $k\ge1$, $\mu=e^{-S/k}$, $L=1-\mu\le t_0$ and $\mu^{1/4}<\theta<1$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ with its supremum norm, set $a_n(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(nS/k-\log(1-t))$, $A_nz(t)=2\int_0^tK(t-r)(a_n(r),z(r))\,dr$, $\Gamma x(t)=G(t)x$, and $Ev=D_\mu v(L)$. It gives $\|A_n\|\le1/4$, a finite-dimensional $V\subset X$, a bounded linear $J:X\to X$ with range in $C$, and a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to X\times\ell^\infty(Y)$. Writing $(e,z)=\mathcal Rg$, the conclusions are $e\in V$, $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$ and $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. The physical datum correction is $Je\in J(V)$; its bound also uses $\|J\|$. The chosen short-interval weight satisfies $e^{-S/(4k)}<\theta<1$. Consequently $\Theta=\theta^k$ lies in $(e^{-S/4},1)$ and $\kappa=-(k/S)\log\theta$ lies in $(0,1/4)$. The paper names $\kappa$ and the whole-period weight explicitly; the formal assertion names $k$ and $\theta$ and does not introduce a global weighted curve norm.

ties.plain: A right inverse for the linearized equations on interval sequences

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $k\ge1$, $\theta>0$, and let $\rho:X\to X$ be a surjective linear isometry. Let $A_n:Y\to Y$, $\Gamma:X\to Y$, $E:Y\to X$ and $J,P:X\to X$ be bounded linear maps. Assume $I-A_n$ have uniformly bounded inverses. Set $S_n=E(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$ and $M=\rho^{-1}S_{k-1}\cdots S_0$, and assume $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, $P^2=P$, $PM=MP$, $PJ=P$. For $0\le r_1<\theta^k<r_2$, require $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$, $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for all $n\ge0,x\in X$, and surjectivity of $M$ on $\operatorname{ran}P$. The formal assertion supplies a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to X\times\ell^\infty(Y)$. For $(e,z)=\mathcal Rg$, it states $e\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$ and $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. The product norm is $\max(\|e\|,\sup_n\|z_n\|_Y)$. The formal assertion begins with the interval operators, their twisted periodicity and spectral bounds. It then specifies an inverse of that sequence problem. The paper's sentence announces the derivation of interval operators from a given global forced curve; this derivation is not a conclusion of the linked assertion.

assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $k\ge1$, $\theta>0$, and let $\rho:X\to X$ be a surjective linear isometry. Set $S_n=E(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$ and $M=\rho^{-1}S_{k-1}\cdots S_0$, and assume $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, $P^2=P$, $PM=MP$, $PJ=P$. For $0\le r_1<\theta^k<r_2$, require $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$, $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for all $n\ge0,x\in X$, and surjectivity of $M$ on $\operatorname{ran}P$. ties.name: Breakdown.StepDataStatement
ties.plain: Interval splitting and right-inverse data for the linearized equation

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space. Suppose $G(t)$, $t\ge0$, is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K(\tau)$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous on each pair of arguments for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $\mu>0$, suppose the dilations are strongly continuous, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For a dense set of $f\in X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with $G,K,D$, including their assigned values at all real parameters. Let $S>0$ and let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to exist and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. For a dense linear subspace $C\subset X$ and $t_0>0$, the formal assertion chooses $k\ge1$, $\mu=e^{-S/k}$, $L=1-\mu\le t_0$ and $\mu^{1/4}<\theta<1$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ with its supremum norm, set $a_n(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(nS/k-\log(1-t))$, $A_nz(t)=2\int_0^tK(t-r)(a_n(r),z(r))\,dr$, $\Gamma x(t)=G(t)x$, and $Ev=D_\mu v(L)$. It gives $\|A_n\|\le1/4$, a finite-dimensional $V\subset X$, a bounded linear $J:X\to X$ with range in $C$, and a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to X\times\ell^\infty(Y)$. Writing $(e,z)=\mathcal Rg$, the conclusions are $e\in V$, $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$ and $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. The formal assertion contains no such global source norm, no formula for that derived forcing, and no claim of the displayed constant's independence from $\chi$.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $k\ge1$, $\theta>0$, and let $\rho:X\to X$ be a surjective linear isometry. rows.fidelity_note: Let $X,E$ be real Banach spaces, $0<L\le1$, $0<\theta<1$, $c\in\mathbb R$, and $C_K\ge0$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ put $B_n(f,g)(t)=\int_0^tK_n(t-r)(f(r),g(r))\,dr$ and $\Gamma_nx(t)=G_n(t)x$. Assume $a_n,r_n\in Y$, $\sup_n\|a_n\|_Y<\infty$, $a_n=\Gamma_na_n(0)+B_n(a_n,a_n)+r_n$, $\|r_n\|_Y\le\theta^n\rho$, and $a_{n+1}(0)=c\,a_n(L)$. rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. rows.fidelity_note: Let $Z$ be a complete normed abelian group, $\Phi:Z\to Z$, and $b,K\ge0$ with $8Kb\le1$. The formal theorem assumes $\|\Phi(z)\|\le b+K\|z\|^2$ for every $z$ and $\|\Phi(z)-\Phi(w)\|\le K(\|z\|+\|w\|)\|z-w\|$ for every $z,w$. It proves that some $z$ satisfies $\Phi(z)=z$ and $\|z\|\le2b$. To use this theorem in the paper, $Z$ must be its complete weighted curve space and $\Phi$ the second component of the right-inverse image of the quadratic expression. Establishing the weighted Duhamel bounds is a separate step; they are not proved by this fixed-point theorem.

assessments.fidelity_note: For a real normed space $X$, the formal heat-flow condition requires bounded linear $G(t)$ with $G(0)=I$, the semigroup law, strong continuity for $t\ge0$, and $\|G(t)\|\le1$ for every $t\ge0$. rows.fidelity_note: Let $X,E$ be real Banach spaces, $0<L\le1$, $0<\theta<1$, $c\in\mathbb R$, and $C_K\ge0$. For each $n$, suppose $G_n$ is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K_n$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous for positive lag, with $G_n(s)K_n(\tau)=K_n(s+\tau)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K_n(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ put $B_n(f,g)(t)=\int_0^tK_n(t-r)(f(r),g(r))\,dr$ and $\Gamma_nx(t)=G_n(t)x$. Assume $a_n,r_n\in Y$, $\sup_n\|a_n\|_Y<\infty$, $a_n=\Gamma_na_n(0)+B_n(a_n,a_n)+r_n$, $\|r_n\|_Y\le\theta^n\rho$, and $a_{n+1}(0)=c\,a_n(L)$. For bounded linear $J:E\to X$, require a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to E\times\ell^\infty(Y)$ which sends $g$ to $(e,z)$ satisfying $z_0-2B_0(a_0,z_0)-\Gamma_0Je=g_0$ and $z_n-2B_n(a_n,z_n)-(c/\theta)\Gamma_nz_{n-1}(L)=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. If $\xi\in X$ obeys $64\|\mathcal R\|^2C_KL^{1/4}(\rho+\|\xi\|)\le1$, the formal assertion supplies $e$ and $z_n$ with $\max(\|e\|,\sup_n\|z_n\|_Y)\le2\|\mathcal R\|(\rho+\|\xi\|)$. The curves $v_n=a_n+\theta^nz_n$ are exact mild solutions on $[0,L]$, $v_{n+1}(0)=c\,v_n(L)$ and $z_0(0)=\xi+Je$. The formal assertion requires a normed complete correction space $E$ and a bounded inverse controlling both components. In Lemma 4.8, $E$ is only a vector space and the bound is imposed on the curve component alone. The formal source norm also separates residual and datum displacement. assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $k\ge1$, $\theta>0$, and let $\rho:X\to X$ be a surjective linear isometry. For $0\le r_1<\theta^k<r_2$, require $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$, $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for all $n\ge0,x\in X$, and surjectivity of $M$ on $\operatorname{ran}P$. assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X,E$ be real Banach spaces, $0<L\le1$, $0<\theta<1$, $c\in\mathbb R$, and $C_K\ge0$. rows.fidelity_note: Let $Z$ be a complete normed abelian group, $\Phi:Z\to Z$, and $b,K\ge0$ with $8Kb\le1$. The formal theorem assumes $\|\Phi(z)\|\le b+K\|z\|^2$ for every $z$ and $\|\Phi(z)-\Phi(w)\|\le K(\|z\|+\|w\|)\|z-w\|$ for every $z,w$. It proves that some $z$ satisfies $\Phi(z)=z$ and $\|z\|\le2b$. For the paper's application, take $b=C_{\mathcal R}\|e^{t\Delta}\chi-F^{\mathrm a}\|_\kappa$ and $K=CC_{\mathcal R}$ with nonnegative constants. If $C>0$ and $\varepsilon_1=(8C)^{-1}$, (4.23) implies $8Kb\le1$ and the ball radius is $\delta=2b$. The fixed-point theorem does not establish that the heat curve belongs to $C_\kappa$, or verify its two bounds for this particular $\Phi$.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X,E$ be real Banach spaces, $0<L\le1$, $0<\theta<1$, $c\in\mathbb R$, and $C_K\ge0$. For each $n$, suppose $G_n$ is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K_n$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous for positive lag, with $G_n(s)K_n(\tau)=K_n(s+\tau)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K_n(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ put $B_n(f,g)(t)=\int_0^tK_n(t-r)(f(r),g(r))\,dr$ and $\Gamma_nx(t)=G_n(t)x$. Assume $a_n,r_n\in Y$, $\sup_n\|a_n\|_Y<\infty$, $a_n=\Gamma_na_n(0)+B_n(a_n,a_n)+r_n$, $\|r_n\|_Y\le\theta^n\rho$, and $a_{n+1}(0)=c\,a_n(L)$. For bounded linear $J:E\to X$, require a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to E\times\ell^\infty(Y)$ which sends $g$ to $(e,z)$ satisfying $z_0-2B_0(a_0,z_0)-\Gamma_0Je=g_0$ and $z_n-2B_n(a_n,z_n)-(c/\theta)\Gamma_nz_{n-1}(L)=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. The formal assertion includes the interval mild equations, matching and initial-value verification, with separate bounds for residual and datum displacement. rows.fidelity_note:
Assume the radial-potential assertion that every smooth solenoidal $g$ has a smooth potential $A_{x_0,g}$ with $\operatorname{curl}A_{x_0,g}=g$. For every smooth scalar function $\chi:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$, every centre $x_0$ and every smooth solenoidal vector field $g$, the formal statement then proves that $\bar g=\chi g+\nabla\chi\times A_{x_0,g}$ is smooth and $\nabla\cdot\bar g=0$ at every point. Here $A_{x_0,g}(x)=\int_0^1\sigma\,g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)\,d\sigma$. In §5 take $x_0=0$, $g=u^*(t)$ and $\chi(x)=\eta(x/r)$ with $r>0$. This theorem assumes no support or size conditions on $\chi$ and therefore gives no support radius, no equality on an inner ball, and no norm bound. Its radial-potential premise is proved in the preceding curl theorem.

For a smooth solenoidal field and a smooth scalar cutoff, the formal statement proves that the vector-potential cutoff is smooth and solenoidal; take the centre to be zero and the scalar cutoff to be $\eta(x/r)$.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffDivergenceFree
rows.plain: Taking the curl gives a smooth solenoidal cutoff
rows.annotation: At fixed $t$, take $g=u^*(t)$ and $\chi(x)=\eta(x/r)$. `cutoffDivergenceFree` takes `HomotopyCurl` as input, which for smooth solenoidal $g$ gives a smooth $A$ with $\operatorname{curl}A=g$. Symmetry of the second derivatives of $\chi$ then gives $\operatorname{div}(\nabla\chi\times A)=-\nabla\chi\cdot g$. This cancels the divergence introduced by $\chi g$ and proves the smooth cutoff is solenoidal.

Assume, uniformly in $s,y$, $\|D_y^jW(s,y)\|_{\rm op}\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for the three integer orders $j=0,1,2$, and $|\nabla_yq(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$. These assumptions imply $C\ge0$; recurrence and nonvanishing are not required here. The norm on a first derivative is its operator norm; the paper's pointwise matrix norm is the square root of the sum of the squared column lengths, which is at most $\sqrt3$ times this norm.

Put $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and let $\chi$ be the fixed smooth cutoff with $0\le\chi\le1$, equal to one for $|x-a|\le1/16$ and zero for $|x-a|\ge1/8$. rows.fidelity_note:
This theorem assumes the following analytic representation facts. On the unit torus, every $C^1$ periodic vector field satisfies $\widehat{\partial_jf}(k)=2\pi i k_j\widehat f(k)$. A smooth compactly supported solenoidal field transplanted at $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$ is smooth, unit-periodic, solenoidal, and agrees with its unwrapped dilation on the ball of radius $1/4$ about $(1/2,1/2,1/2)$. The whole-space heat operators form a strongly continuous self-adjoint contraction semigroup for nonnegative time and act by the multiplier $e^{-4\pi^2\max(t,0)|\xi|^2}$ on their Fourier representatives.

The proof also assumes: uniformly bounded measurable matrix multipliers after any invertible real linear frequency change have their stated almost-everywhere $L^2$ action; the direct and inverse $L^2$ Fourier transforms agree with the corresponding integrals on $L^1\cap L^2$; real $L^2$ fields have conjugate-symmetric Fourier transforms; and, when $h(\xi)=2\pi|\xi|g(\xi)$ almost everywhere for solenoidal representatives, the velocity reconstructed from $h$ equals the real inverse Fourier transform of $g$. The main construction supplies these analytic facts before using this theorem.

The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$.

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

Write $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and let $w(x)$ reduce each coordinate of $x$ modulo integers to the cell centered at $a$. For $\mu>0$, the transplanted field is $g_\mu(x)=\mu^{-1/2}g((w(x)-a)/\sqrt\mu)$.

Whole-space restriction to $\bar B_b$ consists of $1_{\bar B_b}\partial_jv$ and $1_{\bar B_b}v$. At an admissible periodic scale $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt\mu\,b\le1/8$, periodic restriction consists of $1_{\bar B_b}\mu^{3/4}\partial_jz(a+\sqrt\mu\,y)$ and $1_{\bar B_b}\mu^{1/4}z(a+\sqrt\mu\,y)$, interpreted almost everywhere. It is defined to be zero if these scale conditions fail.

For every smooth compactly supported solenoidal field $\varphi$, and every $b,\varepsilon,\delta>0$, the formal statement asserts the existence of $\mu_0>0$ such that, for $0<\mu<\mu_0$ and $0\le\tau\le\varepsilon^{-1}$, the local-data norm of the difference between the restrictions of $e^{\tau\Delta}\varphi$ and $\mu^{1/4}e^{\mu\tau\Delta}\varphi_\mu$ is at most $\delta$. This is uniform convergence on a bounded time interval, including time zero. The threshold can depend on $\varphi$ and no bound proportional to $\|\varphi\|_1$ is asserted. Formula (6.3) instead gives a uniform explicit $L^{-5/2}$ estimate for all $t>0$.

Assume, uniformly in $s,y$, $\|D_y^jW(s,y)\|_{\rm op}\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for the three integer orders $j=0,1,2$, and $|\nabla_yq(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$. These assumptions imply $C\ge0$; recurrence and nonvanishing are not required here. ties.plain: Rescaled approximate solutions match at interval endpoints

rows.fidelity_note:
Assume that $W:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ and $q:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ are smooth, that $\operatorname{div}W=0$, and that $\partial_sW+\tfrac12W+\tfrac12(y\cdot\nabla)W-\Delta W+(W\cdot\nabla)W+\nabla q=0$ for every $(s,y)$. A single constant $C$ bounds $\|D^jW(s,y)\|\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for the integer orders $j=0,1,2$, and $|\nabla q(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$, uniformly in $s$. The norms of $D^jW$ are multilinear operator norms; for $j=1$ the paper’s Frobenius norm is between the operator norm and $\sqrt3$ times that norm.

The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

For $T>0$ and $t<T$, put $s=\log(T/(T-t))$ and $u_T^*(t,x)=(T-t)^{-1/2}W(s,(x-a)/\sqrt{T-t})$, where $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$. Choose a fixed smooth cutoff $\chi$, equal to one on $\bar B_{1/16}(a)$ and zero when $|x-a|\ge1/8$. Put $A_g(x)=\int_0^1\tau g(a+\tau(x-a))\times(x-a)\,d\tau$. The cutoff is $\bar u_T=\chi u_T^*+\nabla\chi\times A_{u_T^*}$, which equals $\operatorname{curl}(\chi A_{u_T^*})$ when $u_T^*$ is solenoidal.

Write $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$, $t_n=T-\mu_n$, $\ell=1-\lambda$, and $a_n(s)=\mu_n^{1/4}u^{\mathrm a}(t_n+\mu_ns)$ for $0\le s\le\ell$, where $u^{\mathrm a}$ is the unit-periodic extension of the solenoidal cutoff of the centered self-similar field. The index $n$ is a nonnegative integer and the interval norm is the supremum norm.

For $0<T\le1$ and $0<\lambda<1$, the formal statement proves the defining formula for every $a_n$ throughout $[0,\ell]$ and the endpoint identity $a_{n+1}(0)=\lambda^{1/4}a_n(\ell)$. The time intervals are $[T-T\lambda^n,T-T\lambda^{n+1}]$, and the factor in the endpoint identity comes from their amplitude normalizations. Values used outside a closed interval are extended by the endpoint values. This supplies the matching needed to assemble continuous physical curves.

The formal theorem establishes continuous normalized interval representatives and their endpoint matching for the scaled unit-periodic approximation. The paper’s sentence concerns the unperiodized cutoff as one whole-space curve.

rows.annotation: For smooth solenoidal $g$ supported in $\bar B_b$, $0<\mu\le1$, $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$, the transplant satisfies $\|\mu^{1/4}g_\mu\|_{H^1(\mathbb T^3)}^2=\int|\nabla g|^2+\mu\int|g|^2$. Unlike (6.1), it includes an $L^2$ term and amplitude normalization. This records the assertion only. The support restriction corresponds to the small-scale condition $\sqrt\mu\,b\le1/8$. The formal periodic norm includes $\mu\|g\|_2^2$ in its square, so it is not the homogeneous isometry stated here.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.torusOp
ties.plain: Linearized interval operator on the torus

assessments.fidelity_note:
The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

Assume a constant $C_{\mathbb T}>0$ with $\|K_{\mathbb T}(\tau)\|\le C_{\mathbb T}\tau^{-3/4}$ for every $0<\tau\le1$. Fix $0<T\le1$, $0<\lambda\le1$, a real $\theta$, a normed datum space $E$, a bounded linear map $J:E\to H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb T^3)$, and a sequence $f_n$ of continuous curves on $[0,1-\lambda]$. Put $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$. On a bounded sequence $z=(z_n)$, the formal definition is $\mathcal L(e,z)=z-Sz-Ge-2\mathcal B(f,z)$. For $n=0$, $(Ge)_0(s)=e^{Ts\Delta}Je$ and $(Sz)_0=0$; for $n\ge1$, $(Sz)_n(s)=(\lambda^{1/4}/\theta)e^{\mu_ns\Delta}z_{n-1}(1-\lambda)$ and $(Ge)_n=0$. The interval bilinear term is $\mathcal B_n(f,z)(s)=\int_0^s\mu_n^{3/4}K_{\mathbb T}(\mu_n(s-\sigma))(f(\sigma),z(\sigma))\,d\sigma$. The pointwise interpretation of the last term requires the family to be bounded; the general definition uses zero for a family that fails to define a bounded sequence operator. Division by zero is set to zero, so using this as a weighted linearization requires $\theta>0$.

In the application $\lambda^{1/4}<\theta<1$ and $f_n$ is uniformly bounded. Formula (6.6) instead combines the same roles in a single physical trajectory.

The formal linearization acts on a sequence of normalized intervals and separately subtracts previous-interval propagation, initial-data heat flow and the bilinear interaction. Formula (6.6) is the corresponding single-trajectory operator.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.ShellInverseTransfer
ties.plain: Transfer of a bounded right inverse from ℝ³ to 𝕋³

rows.fidelity_note:
Let $E,Y,Y_{\mathbb T},Z$ be real Banach spaces. Take bounded linear maps $S:Y\to Y$, $G:E\to Y$, $B:Z\to Y$, $R:Y\to Z$, and corresponding bounded linear periodic maps $S_{\mathbb T},G_{\mathbb T},B_{\mathbb T},R_{\mathbb T}$. Define $\mathcal L(e,y)=y-Sy-Ge-BRy$ and its periodic counterpart. Assume $0\le q<1$, $\|S\|,\|S_{\mathbb T}\|\le q$, and a bounded linear right inverse $F:Y\to E\times Y$ with $\mathcal LF=I$ and $\|F\|\le K$. Suppose the two operator differences $R_{\mathbb T}(I-S_{\mathbb T})^{-1}B_{\mathbb T}-R(I-S)^{-1}B$ and $R_{\mathbb T}(I-S_{\mathbb T})^{-1}G_{\mathbb T}-R(I-S)^{-1}G$ each have norm at most $\delta$, and $4\delta[1+K\|B\|(1+\|R\|)]\le1$.

The formal statement asserts an exact periodic right inverse $F_{\mathbb T}$ with norm at most $(1-q)^{-1}\{1+2(\|B_{\mathbb T}\|+\|G_{\mathbb T}\|+1)[1+K\|B\|(1+\|R\|)]\|R_{\mathbb T}\|(1-q)^{-1}\}$. Product spaces use the maximum norm.

The strict contraction hypotheses make the displayed inverses ordinary bounded inverses and make $1-q$ nonzero. This transfers an inverse through local comparisons; it does not assert the paper’s formula (6.12) or its explicit defect rate.

The formal assertion transfers an exact right inverse using two small localized operator differences and an explicit algebraic inequality. It does not export this particular candidate map or the $L^{-1/2}$ defect rate.

rows.plain: Transfer of a bounded right inverse from ℝ³ to 𝕋³

Not (6.12). `ShellInverseTransfer` transfers an exact right inverse using two small localized operator differences and an explicit algebraic inequality. It does not export this particular candidate map or the $L^{-1/2}$ defect rate.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.restrictTorus
ties.plain: Restriction of a periodic velocity

rows.fidelity_note:
The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

Whole-space restriction to $\bar B_b$ consists of $1_{\bar B_b}\partial_jv$ and $1_{\bar B_b}v$. Write $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ for the fixed centre of the unit cell. At an admissible periodic scale $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt\mu\,b\le1/8$, periodic restriction consists of $1_{\bar B_b}\mu^{3/4}\partial_jz(a+\sqrt\mu\,y)$ and $1_{\bar B_b}\mu^{1/4}z(a+\sqrt\mu\,y)$, interpreted almost everywhere. It is defined to be zero if these scale conditions fail.

This is a bounded linear map for every real pair $(\mu,b)$. The derivatives and velocity are recovered from Fourier series in $L^2$ and $L^6$, respectively. The derivative entries are restrictions of the derivatives of the original field; they are not asserted to be the distributional derivatives of its zero extension. It records local values and derivative values as independent coordinates, so its target is larger than the image of $H^1(B)$. On admissible scales the normalized local norms are bounded by a constant times the unit-torus $H^1$ norm, uniformly in the admissible scale. The paper instead restricts an unscaled field on a large torus and uses the sum of the gradient and velocity norms.

The formal periodic restriction first evaluates at $a+\sqrt\mu\,y$ and applies factors $\mu^{1/4}$ to values and $\mu^{3/4}$ to derivatives. Its target records separate local entries, and it is zero at inadmissible scales.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.RestrictR3Bound
ties.plain: Uniform bound for restricting ℝ³ velocities and gradients

assessments.fidelity_note:
The periodic space is the real solenoidal $H^1$ space on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. The zero Fourier coefficient is allowed. The whole-space space $X$ consists of solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$ with norm $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_2$.

Local data form the space $Z=(L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3))^3\times L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ with norm $\|(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)\|_Z=\max\{\|A_1\|_2,\|A_2\|_2,\|A_3\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. Its entries are equivalence classes modulo equality almost everywhere. General tuples have neither the compatibility $A_j=\partial_jv$ nor a divergence condition.

For every real $b$, whole-space restriction is $R_bv=(1_{\bar B_b}\partial_1v,1_{\bar B_b}\partial_2v,1_{\bar B_b}\partial_3v,1_{\bar B_b}v)$. The formal statement gives one $C\ge0$ with $\|R_b\|_{X\to Z}\le C$ for all real $b$. If $b\le0$, these entries are zero almost everywhere. The derivative entries restrict the original derivatives; they need not be derivatives of the zero-extended velocity.

The formal assertion gives a radius-independent bound for the whole-space restriction into the maximum norm of local derivative and value entries. The paper uses their sum as an $H^1(B)$ norm and also states a periodic estimate.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.operatorNormBounds_holds
ties.plain: Uniform bounds for restriction, transplant and local Duhamel maps

rows.fidelity_note:
The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$.

The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

An approximation on $[0,\ell]$ is specified, for every integer $n\ge0$, by a finite sum $A_n(s)=\sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_{n,j}(s)\varphi_{n,j}$, where each $\alpha_{n,j}$ is continuous, each $\varphi_{n,j}$ is smooth, compactly supported and solenoidal with support in $\bar B_b$, and both the weights and $\|\varphi_{n,j}\|_X$ have one uniform bound. The number $m$ is fixed.

The formal statement proves that one $C\ge0$ bounds the whole-space and periodic localized Duhamel operators by $CM$, if $\sup_n\|A_n\|_{C([0,\ell];X)}\le M$, and bounds the whole-space and scaled periodic restriction operators by $C$. For the whole-space Duhamel estimate $0<\ell\le1$; restriction alone only requires $\ell>0$. The periodic estimates assume $0<T\le1$, $0<\lambda<1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt T b\le1/8$ and $\ell=1-\lambda$. Restriction records the value with factor $\mu_n^{1/4}$ and each derivative with factor $\mu_n^{3/4}$ after $x=a+\sqrt{\mu_n}y$, where $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$ and $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$. The same statement bounds the previous-interval heat propagation operator by $\lambda^{1/4}/\theta$, for $\theta>0$. In the whole-space formula $\lambda=e^{-P/k}$ with $P>0$ and positive integer $k$; the periodic propagation bound allows $0<\lambda\le1$. Thus the propagation is a strict contraction when $\lambda^{1/4}<\theta$. These are supremum norms on interval sequences, rather than the paper’s continuous $C_\kappa$ norm.

Bounded linear restriction gives continuous local-data curves in the formal representation. The target tuple space imposes no divergence or derivative-compatibility condition; those properties belong to the original field.

rows.annotation: Local data are tuples $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2$ and $v\in L^6$, normed by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. Unlike the paper's restriction of one $H^1(B)$ velocity, the tuples need not satisfy $A_j=\partial_jv$ or any divergence condition. The formal local data allow arbitrary $L^2$ derivative entries and an $L^6$ velocity entry. Requiring that they come from one divergence-free $H^1(B)$ curve is an extra restriction made in the paper.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.advectShell
ties.plain: The localized transport term

rows.fidelity_note: When the local tuple is the velocity and its actual derivatives, the formal definition is the same symmetrized transport field extended by zero. It uses the closed ball, whose boundary does not change the represented $L^2$ field.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.advectShell
rows.plain: The localized transport term
rows.annotation: For a test field $\varphi$ and local data $\zeta=(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$, defines the $L^2$ field $1_{\bar B_b}\sum_j(\varphi_jA_j+v_j\partial_j\varphi)$. When $A_j=\partial_jv$ it is the paper's $(\varphi\cdot\nabla)v+(v\cdot\nabla)\varphi$ extended by zero. When the local tuple is the velocity and its actual derivatives, the formal definition is the same symmetrized transport field extended by zero. It uses the closed ball, whose boundary does not change the represented $L^2$ field.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.AdvectShellBounds
ties.plain: Uniform bound on linearized convection in the local shell

assessments.fidelity_note:
The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$.

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

For every $\varphi\in C^\infty_{c,\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb R^3)$, every real $b$, and every local tuple $\zeta=(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$, put $f=1_{\bar B_b}\sum_j(\varphi_jA_j+v_j\partial_j\varphi)$.

The formal statement asserts a constant $C\ge0$, independent of these inputs, such that $\|f\|_{3/2}\le C\|\varphi\|_X\|\zeta\|$, and asserts that $f$ vanishes almost everywhere outside $\bar B_b$. The estimate applies without requiring $A_j=\partial_jv$ or $\operatorname{div}v=0$. Its time dependence in (6.8) is obtained only after substituting the bound for the chosen time-dependent background.

The formal estimate is $\|f\|_{3/2}\le C\|\varphi\|_X\|\zeta\|$ for arbitrary local tuples. The paper’s factor $(1-t)^{-1/4}$ uses the separate norm bound for the chosen time-dependent cutoff, and its local norm is a sum.
