ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.r3Lambda
ties.plain: The localized Duhamel operator

rows.fidelity_note:
The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$.

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

An approximation on $[0,\ell]$ is specified, for every integer $n\ge0$, by a finite sum $A_n(s)=\sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_{n,j}(s)\varphi_{n,j}$, where each $\alpha_{n,j}$ is continuous, each $\varphi_{n,j}$ is smooth, compactly supported and solenoidal with support in $\bar B_b$, and both the weights and $\|\varphi_{n,j}\|_X$ have one uniform bound. The number $m$ is fixed.

For a bounded sequence of continuous local curves $\zeta_n$, the operator acts on interval $n$ as $\sum_j\int_0^s\alpha_{n,j}(\sigma)\Lambda_{\varphi_{n,j}}(s-\sigma)\zeta_n(\sigma)\,d\sigma$, where $\Lambda_\varphi(\tau)\zeta=-e^{\tau\Delta}\mathbb P[1_{\bar B_b}\sum_i(\varphi_iA_i+v_i\partial_i\varphi)]$. The domain and range have the supremum norm over $n$ and $s$. The displayed integral interpretation is proved for $0<\ell\le1$ using the $\tau^{-3/4}$ estimate and continuity for positive lags.

The general definition selects the bounded linear map with this formula if it exists and uses zero otherwise; the analytic estimates exclude that alternative in the application. This assembles localized interactions of finite-sum approximations, rather than the paper’s one global curve $\bar u$.

The formal whole-space operator integrates localized interactions of finite sums of compact smooth fields on each normalized interval, then forms a bounded sequence. The paper fixes one cutoff field on the entire physical interval.

It assembles finite-sum approximations, not one global curve $\bar u$. rows.fidelity_note:
The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

An approximation on $[0,\ell]$ is specified, for every integer $n\ge0$, by a finite sum $A_n(s)=\sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_{n,j}(s)\varphi_{n,j}$, where each $\alpha_{n,j}$ is continuous, each $\varphi_{n,j}$ is smooth, compactly supported and solenoidal with support in $\bar B_b$, and both the weights and $\|\varphi_{n,j}\|_X$ have one uniform bound. The number $m$ is fixed.

Put $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$ with $0<T\le1$ and $0<\lambda<1$, and assume $b>0$, $\sqrt T b\le1/8$ and $0<\ell\le1$. The operator on a bounded sequence of local curves is $\sum_j\int_0^s\alpha_{n,j}(\sigma)\Lambda^{(\mu_n)}_{\varphi_{n,j}}(s-\sigma)\zeta_n(\sigma)\,d\sigma$ on interval $n$. Here $\Lambda^{(\mu)}_\varphi(\tau)\zeta=-\mu^{-1/4}e^{\mu\tau\Delta}\mathbb P[f_\zeta((w(x)-a)/\sqrt\mu)]$, with $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$, coordinate reduction $w$, and $f_\zeta=1_{\bar B_b}\sum_i(\varphi_iA_i+v_i\partial_i\varphi)$. Both sequence norms are suprema in $n$ and in interval time. The construction uses zero when the required bounded integral map does not exist; the scale hypotheses and the heat estimate establish the integral formula here. This is the interval version of the paper’s $\mathcal A_{\mathbb T}$.

The formal periodic operator uses the unit torus with scale $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$ in each interval. The paper integrates on a torus of fixed large period with one physical-time curve.

rows.plain: The periodic Duhamel operator
rows.annotation: `torusLambda` defines the periodic interval operator: on interval $n$, with $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$, it integrates the weighted rescaled torus projected heat flow of the transplanted transport term against the local curve. It is the interval version of the paper's $\mathcal A_{\mathbb T}$. The formal periodic operator uses the unit torus with scale $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$ in each interval. The paper integrates on a torus of fixed large period with one physical-time curve.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.r3LambdaBound_holds
ties.plain: Local whole-space Duhamel estimate for projected forcing

rows.fidelity_note:
The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$.

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

For every $\varphi\in C^\infty_{c,\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb R^3)$, real $b$, $\tau>0$ and local tuple $\zeta=(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$, define $f_\zeta=1_{\bar B_b}\sum_j(\varphi_jA_j+v_j\partial_j\varphi)$.

The formal statement proves a constant $C\ge0$ such that $\|e^{\tau\Delta}\mathbb Pf_\zeta\|_X\le C\tau^{-3/4}\|\varphi\|_X\|\zeta\|$. The constant is independent of $b,\tau,\varphi,\zeta$, and no relation between the derivative entries and the velocity entry is assumed. This is a fixed-lag estimate; integrability and continuity of the Duhamel integral require the time-dependent inputs.

The formal whole-space estimate bounds the localized projected heat field by $C\tau^{-3/4}\|\varphi\|_X\|\zeta\|$. The paper first estimates by the $L^{3/2}$ norm of the assembled transport forcing.

ties.plain: Uniform bounds for restriction, transplant and local Duhamel maps

rows.fidelity_note:
The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$.

An approximation on $[0,\ell]$ is specified, for every integer $n\ge0$, by a finite sum $A_n(s)=\sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_{n,j}(s)\varphi_{n,j}$, where each $\alpha_{n,j}$ is continuous, each $\varphi_{n,j}$ is smooth, compactly supported and solenoidal with support in $\bar B_b$, and both the weights and $\|\varphi_{n,j}\|_X$ have one uniform bound. The formal statement proves that one $C\ge0$ bounds the whole-space and periodic localized Duhamel operators by $CM$, if $\sup_n\|A_n\|_{C([0,\ell];X)}\le M$, and bounds the whole-space and scaled periodic restriction operators by $C$. For the whole-space Duhamel estimate $0<\ell\le1$; restriction alone only requires $\ell>0$. The periodic estimates assume $0<T\le1$, $0<\lambda<1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt T b\le1/8$ and $\ell=1-\lambda$. assessments.fidelity_note:
The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$. 

The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero. 

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space. 

An approximation on $[0,\ell]$ is specified, for every integer $n\ge0$, by a finite sum $A_n(s)=\sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_{n,j}(s)\varphi_{n,j}$, where each $\alpha_{n,j}$ is continuous, each $\varphi_{n,j}$ is smooth, compactly supported and solenoidal with support in $\bar B_b$, and both the weights and $\|\varphi_{n,j}\|_X$ have one uniform bound. The number $m$ is fixed. 

Use the whole-space heat flow, Navier–Stokes bilinear kernel and spatial dilation $D_\lambda f(x)=\lambda^{1/2}f(\lambda^{1/2}x)$, and assume the periodic kernel estimate $\|K_{\mathbb T}(\tau)\|\le C_{\mathbb T}\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. Let $P>0$, let $k>0$ be an integer, put $\lambda=e^{-P/k}$ and $\ell=1-\lambda\le1/2$, and choose $\lambda^{1/4}<\theta<1$ and $b>0$. The preceding finite-sum approximation is taken on $[0,\ell]$. Let $E$ be finite dimensional, let $J:E\to X$ be bounded linear, and let $e\mapsto\psi_e$ be linear, with each $\psi_e$ smooth, compactly supported, solenoidal, supported in $\bar B_b$, and representing $Je$.

The three spaces used below are the bounded sequences of continuous $X$-valued, periodic-$H^1$-valued and local-data-valued curves on $[0,\ell]$. Each has norm $\sup_n\sup_{0\le s\le\ell}\|v_n(s)\|$. Write $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$, let $w$ reduce coordinates to the unit cell centered at $a$, and put $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$. The periodic datum map is $J_{\mathbb T}e=T^{1/4}(\psi_e)_T$, where $(\psi_e)_T(x)=T^{-1/2}\psi_e((w(x)-a)/\sqrt T)$.

Here are the operators whose differences the formal statement controls. Whole-space restriction $R$ records $1_{\bar B_b}\partial_jv_n$ and $1_{\bar B_b}v_n$. Periodic restriction $R_{\mathbb T}$ records $1_{\bar B_b}\mu_n^{3/4}\partial_jz_n(a+\sqrt{\mu_n}y)$ and $1_{\bar B_b}\mu_n^{1/4}z_n(a+\sqrt{\mu_n}y)$. The periodic restriction is zero if $0<\mu_n\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt{\mu_n}b\le1/8$ fail; sufficiently small $T$ ensures these conditions. For a local tuple $\zeta=(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ put $F_{\varphi,\zeta}=1_{\bar B_b}\sum_j(\varphi_jA_j+v_j\partial_j\varphi)$. The whole-space interaction is
$\displaystyle (B\zeta)_n(s)=-\sum_l\int_0^s\alpha_{n,l}(\sigma)e^{(s-\sigma)\Delta}\mathbb PF_{\varphi_{n,l},\zeta_n(\sigma)}\,d\sigma.$
For $B_{\mathbb T}$ replace the projected heat field under the integral by
$\displaystyle \mu_n^{-1/4}e^{\mu_n(s-\sigma)\Delta}\mathbb P\bigl[F_{\varphi_{n,l},\zeta_n(\sigma)}((w(x)-a)/\sqrt{\mu_n})\bigr].$
The minus sign and weights are unchanged. These definitions use the bounded integral operators supplied by the heat estimates; their general definitions assign zero if the required bounded realization does not exist.

The preceding-interval maps satisfy $(Sy)_0=(S_{\mathbb T}z)_0=0$ and, for $n\ge1$,
$\displaystyle (Sy)_n(s)=\theta^{-1}e^{s\Delta}D_\lambda y_{n-1}(\ell),\qquad (S_{\mathbb T}z)_n(s)=\frac{\lambda^{1/4}}\theta e^{\mu_ns\Delta}z_{n-1}(\ell).$
The datum maps have $(Ge)_0(s)=e^{s\Delta}Je$ and $(G_{\mathbb T}e)_0(s)=e^{Ts\Delta}J_{\mathbb T}e$, with all later entries zero. The propagation bounds are $\|S\|,\|S_{\mathbb T}\|\le\lambda^{1/4}/\theta<1$, so $I-S$ and $I-S_{\mathbb T}$ have ordinary bounded inverses. The general inverse convention assigns zero to a noninvertible operator, which is excluded here.

For every $\delta>0$, the formal statement asserts a $T_0>0$ such that, for every $0<T\le1$ with $T<T_0$, and the datum map just specified,
$\displaystyle \|R_{\mathbb T}(I-S_{\mathbb T})^{-1}B_{\mathbb T}-R(I-S)^{-1}B\|\le\delta,\qquad \|R_{\mathbb T}(I-S_{\mathbb T})^{-1}G_{\mathbb T}-R(I-S)^{-1}G\|\le\delta.$
The threshold is uniform in the sequence index. No explicit rate in $T$ or the paper’s large torus period is asserted.

The formal assertion bounds two localized operator differences by a prescribed $\delta$ for sufficiently small $T$. It does not state the bound $CL^{-1/2}\|g\|_\kappa$ for the displayed candidate inverse.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.freeHeatComparison
ties.plain: Free heat flow converges locally in the small-scale torus limit

rows.fidelity_note:
This theorem assumes the following analytic representation facts. On the unit torus, every $C^1$ periodic vector field satisfies $\widehat{\partial_jf}(k)=2\pi i k_j\widehat f(k)$. A smooth compactly supported solenoidal field transplanted at $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$ is smooth, unit-periodic, solenoidal, and agrees with its unwrapped dilation on the ball of radius $1/4$ about $(1/2,1/2,1/2)$. The whole-space heat operators form a strongly continuous self-adjoint contraction semigroup for nonnegative time and act by the multiplier $e^{-4\pi^2\max(t,0)|\xi|^2}$ on their Fourier representatives.

The proof also assumes: uniformly bounded measurable matrix multipliers after any invertible real linear frequency change have their stated almost-everywhere $L^2$ action; the direct and inverse $L^2$ Fourier transforms agree with the corresponding integrals on $L^1\cap L^2$; real $L^2$ fields have conjugate-symmetric Fourier transforms; and, when $h(\xi)=2\pi|\xi|g(\xi)$ almost everywhere for solenoidal representatives, the velocity reconstructed from $h$ equals the real inverse Fourier transform of $g$. The main construction supplies these analytic facts before using this theorem.

The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$.

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

rows.fidelity_note:

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation
ties.plain: Correcting a periodic approximate flow on all time intervals

rows.fidelity_note:
Let $X$ and $E$ be arbitrary real Banach spaces. Fix $0<\ell\le1$, $0<\theta<1$, a real endpoint factor $c$, $C_K\ge0$, and a bounded datum map $J:E\to X$. For each nonnegative integer $n$, let $G_n$ and $K_n$ be a strongly continuous contraction heat semigroup and a symmetric bilinear kernel with positive-lag continuity, $G_n(a)K_n(\tau)=K_n(a+\tau)$ for $a\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|K_n(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. Write $\mathcal B_n(f,g)(s)=\int_0^sK_n(s-\sigma)(f(\sigma),g(\sigma))\,d\sigma$.

Take continuous $a_n,r_n:[0,\ell]\to X$, uniformly bounded $a_n$, with $a_{n+1}(0)=ca_n(\ell)$,
$\displaystyle a_n=G_n(\cdot)a_n(0)+\mathcal B_n(a_n,a_n)+r_n,\qquad\|r_n\|_\infty\le\theta^n\rho.$
Suppose a bounded linear map $R:\ell^\infty(C([0,\ell];X))\to E\times\ell^\infty(C([0,\ell];X))$ has the following right-inverse property: for each $g$, if $(e,z)=Rg$, then
$\displaystyle z_0-2\mathcal B_0(a_0,z_0)-G_0(\cdot)Je=g_0,$
$\displaystyle z_n-2\mathcal B_n(a_n,z_n)-(c/\theta)G_n(\cdot)z_{n-1}(\ell)=g_n\quad(n\ge1).$
The sequence norm is the supremum over $n$ and interval time, and the product norm is the maximum norm. For $\xi\in X$, assume $64\|R\|^2C_K\ell^{1/4}(\rho+\|\xi\|)\le1$. The formal assertion gives $e\in E$ and continuous curves $z_n$, each bounded in norm by $2\|R\|(\rho+\|\xi\|)$, with the same bound for $\|e\|$, such that $a_n+\theta^nz_n$ is exactly mild on $[0,\ell]$, the corrected endpoints match with factor $c$, and $z_0(0)=\xi+Je$. No finite-dimensional hypothesis is imposed on $E$.

The formal correction uses one bound $C_K$ for all normalized interval kernels and the condition $64\|R\|^2C_K\ell^{1/4}(\rho+\|\xi\|)\le1$. It does not state a large-torus family of $C_\kappa$ thresholds.

The periodic space is the real solenoidal $H^1$ space on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. The zero Fourier coefficient is allowed. The whole-space space $X$ consists of solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$ with norm $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_2$.

The formal assertion is that there exist a smooth unit-periodic solenoidal initial field $u_0$, a time $T>0$ and a trajectory $u:\mathbb R\to H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb T^3)$ which is a continuous mild solution on $[0,T)$, starts at the Fourier representation of $u_0$, and has unbounded $H^1$ norm on that interval. Its mild equation is the periodic Duhamel equation with an integrable bilinear term at each time. It specifies neither a correction space nor a two-sided rate nor a norm of the difference from the self-similar profile.

The quoted formula specifies a decomposition, an initial correction and, in (6.17), its weighted bound. The formal assertion omits those identities and adds existential finite-time unboundedness. Neither assertion is the same mathematical claim as the other.

This theorem assumes two analytic properties for every real Banach space with a strongly continuous contraction semigroup $G$ and a symmetric positive-lag continuous bilinear kernel $K$ satisfying $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. First, on every interval $[0,\ell]$, $\ell>0$, the bounded bilinear curve operator is the Duhamel integral, has norm at most $4C_K\ell^{1/4}$ if $\ell\le1$, and the free curve operator is $x\mapsto G(\cdot)x$ with norm at most one. Second, if continuous curves $u,v$ on $[a,b]$, $a\le b$, have bounds $M,N$, their Duhamel integrals from $a$ to $t$ are integrable and continuous for every $t\in[a,b]$, and their norms are at most $4C_K(t-a)^{1/4}MN$ when $t-a\le1$. It proves the interval correction statement below from these two properties. Their proofs are supplied elsewhere in the same source package.

Let $X,E$ be real Banach spaces. For each integer $n\ge0$, let $G_n$ be a strongly continuous contraction heat semigroup and $K_n$ a continuous symmetric bilinear kernel satisfying $G_n(s)K_n(\tau)=K_n(s+\tau)$ for $s\ge0$, $\tau>0$, with $\|K_n(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$, where $C_K\ge0$ is independent of $n$. Fix $0<\ell\le1$, $0<\theta<1$, a real endpoint factor $c$, bounded linear $J:E\to X$, and continuous interval curves $a_n,r_n:[0,\ell]\to X$. Assume $\|a_n\|_\infty\le M$, $a_{n+1}(0)=c\,a_n(\ell)$, $a_n=G_n(\cdot)a_n(0)+\mathcal B_n(a_n,a_n)+r_n$, and $\|r_n\|_\infty\le\theta^n\rho$. Here $\mathcal B_n(f,g)(s)=\int_0^sK_n(s-\sigma)(f(\sigma),g(\sigma))\,d\sigma$.

Suppose a bounded linear map $R$ takes each bounded interval sequence $g$ to $(e,z)$ satisfying $z_n-2\mathcal B_n(a_n,z_n)-G_n(\cdot)Je=g_0$ for $n=0$, and $z_n-2\mathcal B_n(a_n,z_n)-(c/\theta)G_n(\cdot)z_{n-1}(\ell)=g_n$ for $n\ge1$.

For a datum displacement $\xi\in X$, assume $64\|R\|^2C_K\ell^{1/4}(\rho+\|\xi\|)\le1$.

The formal statement proves an $e$ and curves $z_n$ with $\|e\|,\sup_n\|z_n\|_\infty\le2\|R\|(\rho+\|\xi\|)$, such that, on writing $v_n=a_n+\theta^nz_n$, each $v_n$ satisfies $v_n(s)=G_n(s)v_n(0)+\mathcal B_n(v_n,v_n)(s)$ on the closed interval, with an integrable nonlinear term. Moreover $v_{n+1}(0)=c\,v_n(\ell)$ and $z_0(0)=\xi+Je$. The sequence norm and the product norm are maxima. The positive hypotheses exclude zero denominators.

The theorem derives exact corrected intervals and their datum correction from the curve-operator and Duhamel-integral properties. It retains the interval bound, rather than the assembled weighted estimate and datum formula in (6.17).

ties.plain: Uniform upper and positive lower bounds for the periodic pieces

rows.fidelity_note:
Assume that $W:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ and $q:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ are smooth, that $\operatorname{div}W=0$, and that $\partial_sW+\tfrac12W+\tfrac12(y\cdot\nabla)W-\Delta W+(W\cdot\nabla)W+\nabla q=0$ for every $(s,y)$. A single constant $C$ bounds $\|D^jW(s,y)\|\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for the integer orders $j=0,1,2$, and $|\nabla q(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$, uniformly in $s$. The norms of $D^jW$ are multilinear operator norms; for $j=1$ the paper’s Frobenius norm is between the operator norm and $\sqrt3$ times that norm.

The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

For $T>0$ and $t<T$, put $s=\log(T/(T-t))$ and $u_T^*(t,x)=(T-t)^{-1/2}W(s,(x-a)/\sqrt{T-t})$, where $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$. Choose a fixed smooth cutoff $\chi$, equal to one on $\bar B_{1/16}(a)$ and zero when $|x-a|\ge1/8$. Put $A_g(x)=\int_0^1\tau g(a+\tau(x-a))\times(x-a)\,d\tau$. The cutoff is $\bar u_T=\chi u_T^*+\nabla\chi\times A_{u_T^*}$, which equals $\operatorname{curl}(\chi A_{u_T^*})$ when $u_T^*$ is solenoidal.

Write $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$, $t_n=T-\mu_n$, $\ell=1-\lambda$, and $a_n(s)=\mu_n^{1/4}u^{\mathrm a}(t_n+\mu_ns)$ for $0\le s\le\ell$, where $u^{\mathrm a}$ is the unit-periodic extension of the solenoidal cutoff of the centered self-similar field. The index $n$ is a nonnegative integer and the interval norm is the supremum norm.

Assume $0<\lambda<1$ and $c>0$ with $c\le\|W(s)\|_X$ for every real $s$.

The formal statement asserts the existence of $T_0>0$ and $M\in\mathbb R$ such that, for every $0<T<T_0$ and every $n\ge0$, $\|a_n\|_{C([0,\ell];H^1)}\le M$ and $c/2\le\|a_n(s)\|_{H^1}$ for every $0\le s\le\ell$. Here $\|W(s)\|_X=\|\nabla W(s)\|_2$. The curve is represented by its continuous restriction; the general construction uses zero if continuity fails, while the profile hypotheses ensure continuity here. The statement gives no equality with a whole-space homogeneous norm and no explicit factor $c_*-CL^{-1/2}$.

The formal assertion bounds the approximate normalized intervals. It concerns the uncorrected field, so it is an ingredient for this corrected-velocity statement rather than the same conclusion.

rows.annotation: Every $(R,\tau)\in\Gamma$ has $R=R_{a\pi/\kappa}R_*^b$ and $\tau=a/2+j$ for natural $a$, $b\in\{0,1\}$ and integer $j$. rows.annotation: For measurable $E\subset\mathbb R^3$ meeting each positive ray in nothing or in $(a,\infty)$, $a>0$, and real $u\in L^6$ with weak gradient $G\in L^2$, $\int_E|u|^2/|y|^2\le4\int_E|G(y)(y/|y|)|^2$. The complete formal condition includes these two comparisons and also the row-sum residual test, symmetry, positive weights and pivot lower bounds. At one node, let $A=N_\xi+\sum_{\xi'}V_{\xi'}$, with the sum over its children, and let $V_\xi$ be the matrix passed to its parent. Given pivots $\mathcal U_\xi$ and columns $Y_\xi$, the condition supplies symmetric $H,K$, symmetric entrywise nonnegative $H',K'$, positive weights $w_j$, real $p_j,m_j$, and a rectangular real matrix $Y'$. For every real $x$ it requires $\langle Hx,x\rangle\le\langle Ax,x\rangle+\langle H'|x|,|x|\rangle$ and $\langle V_\xi x,x\rangle\le\langle Kx,x\rangle-\sum_{j\notin\mathcal U_\xi}m_jx_j^2+\langle K'|x|,|x|\rangle$. For each row, $w_i\sum_j(|B_{ij}|+H'_{ij}+K'_{ij})/w_j\le m_i$, where $B=H-\operatorname{diag}_{\mathcal U_\xi}(p)-Y'Y'^T+Y_\xi Y_\xi^T-K$ and the diagonal is zero off the pivots. On each pivot $\underline p_{\xi,j}\le p_j-m_j$. Here $|x|$ means componentwise absolute value. All spaces are finite-dimensional and the forms are real. The positive weights exclude zero denominators. These are assumptions on the supplied node matrices and bounds; they perform no numerical verification themselves.

ties.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.IsAdjointField
ties.plain: Periodicity, decay and weak derivatives of adjoint fields

rows.fidelity_note: The formal condition requires a jointly $C^1$, period-one, divergence-free field $\psi$ on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ with $|\psi|\le C(1+|y|)^{-\gamma}$ uniformly in time for some $\gamma>5/2$, together with derivative and weak-second-derivative conditions. With continuity, this decay gives $\psi\in\mathcal H$, the periodic fields square integrable on $(0,1)\times\mathbb R^3$, since $2\gamma>3$. It therefore implies both properties in the paper sentence and also imposes further regularity and decay.
